# odinex_elastic_ip (Resource)

Manages an Elastic IP: a public IPv4 address NATed to a server without public IPs (its primary network needs an `odinex_nat_gateway`). Nothing is configured inside the guest. Assign it with `server_id` or with `odinex_elastic_ip_assignment` (not both).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "odinex_elastic_ip" "app" {
  name     = "app"
  location = "fra1"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `delete_protection` (Boolean) Prevent the resource from being deleted. Defaults to `false`.
- `labels` (Map of String) User-defined labels (key/value pairs). Up to 64 pairs; keys and values up to 63 characters.
- `location` (String) Location of the Elastic IP. Required unless `server_id` is set.
- `name` (String) Name of the Elastic IP.
- `server_id` (Number) Server the IP is assigned to. The server must have no public IPs.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Unique ID of the resource.
- `ip_address` (String) The IP address.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import odinex_elastic_ip.app 9
```
